blocks.content:
The Constitution does NOT specify the tenure. The President determines the period of service.

Members are eligible for reappointment.
The President also determines service conditions.
The Constitution does NOT specify the tenure.

items: Statement-based question alert: The Constitution does NOT fix the tenure; it is determined entirely by the President.
Pay attention to eligibility: Members are eligible for reappointment, which is a common point tested in MCQs.
Do not confuse Parliament with the President: Service conditions are decided by the President.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution does NOT specify the exact tenure for members.
The President holds the authority to determine both the period of service and service conditions.
Members retain eligibility for reappointment after their term.
